dossier.public_summary: The 0.72-day dips track the star's own 0.72-day spot rotation with a large phase-curve swing, shallow depths that fade by ~67% between sectors in the same pipeline, and durations far longer than a planet should have around this 0.21-solar-radius M dwarf. The centroid puts the signal on the star, so it is best explained as stellar variability folding at the spin period, not a planet.

reasons.why: Dip period at star's rotation period with high chi2 phase-curve signal much larger than depth. Best explanation is stellar variability folding at the rotation period, not a planet.
reasons.value: signal_period_d 0.718 vs rotation_d 0.7175, signal_over_rotation 1.000412543554007, amplitude_ppm 23608, 16075, 18943, 13205; chi2 1056 dof 9, amplitude_ppm 7924 ratio_to_depth 1.314

reasons.why: Depth changes within SPOC 2-min and changes_within_a_source verdict for same source, so depth change is not a calibration offset. Sector_depths_by_source shows 5392 ppm +/-278 ppm with p_constant same as global.
Transits much longer than central for very low-mass 0.2119 Rsol star and stellar density mismatch, as expected for spotted/detrended variability not a planet.
reasons.value: observed_h 0.9987 central_h 0.6102 ratio 1.637; stellar_radius TIC 0.212 rad mass 0.181 duration_ratio 1.64 rp_rearth 1.8; per-sector b 1.026e-8 fit_log_density_ratio -2.335

reasons.why: Difference imaging places dip on target and rules out neighbours (no plausible_within_1px) but on_target here means variability on the target, not a planet, as rotation explains signal better.
